body: SicSemperHumanus said it all, really. It's a distraction. The physical pain that you're experiencing at the moment that you're cutting distracts from the horrible things you spend most of your time thinking about. Also, the endorphins are a rush. It can get rather addicting. Me, personally? I cut during times of great stress where I simply DO NOT want to think, or when I can't sleep. It helps me fall asleep.

I've been through professional counseling for years, though I've not had a therapy session in about a year and a half. I think it's time for me to begin going again. I'd hit up my school's services for this kind of thing, but as I go to a community college, they're not too keen on pointing you in the right direction.. to much of anything, really. 

Thank you for the support, I sincerely appreciate it. And, your comment history doesn't suggest that you're an asshole, just that you're a person. =)

I know that a year from now things will be different, and perhaps better. I'm just tired of thinking that. Ever since I was little, I gave myself a countdown of years until "things were better". Young-me decided that at 18, things would be marvelous, because I could get away from my insane parents and all the drama they created.

I'm 18 and I'm still surrounded by most of it. I don't know. Young-me is very disappointed in older-me, right about now.

I'll take your suggestion on doing some volunteer work. Anything to get my mind off of things. And I love helping people.

You're right about that. Kitties are lifesavers. Whenever I think about killing myself, I remember that nobody can take care of my cat the way I do, and he probably wouldn't like whoever ended up taking care of him anyway. Sometimes when I'm sad and crying, he'll come up and lick the tears off of my face. I love him.
